module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 19.25

by B. Curtin, G. R. Pourgholi

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v40)
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Nat Group

namespace Kourovka.«19.25»

/--
Let $G$ and $H$ be finite groups of the same order with
$\sum_{g \in G} \phi(|g|) = \sum_{h \in H} \phi(|h|)$,
where $\phi$ is the Euler totient function. Suppose that $G$ is simple. Is
$H$ necessarily simple?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka_19_25 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H] [Fintype G] [Fintype H],
       Fintype.card G = Fintype.card H →
       ∑ g : G, φ (orderOf g) = ∑ h : H, φ (orderOf h) →
       IsSimpleGroup G → IsSimpleGroup H := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«19.25»

status_issues.source_status: Solved negatively by P. Monticone in a solution note dated 10 May 2026, subsequently detailed in van Doorn–Judin–Monticone–Morrison, arXiv:2607.17477v2.
status_issues.evidence: The latest notebook, https://arxiv.org/html/1401.0300v46#p1030.3, explicitly records: “No, it need not be.” The cited paper constructs G = PSU(3,3), which is simple, and H = C₆ × S₄ × (C₇ ⋊ C₆), which is not simple, where the semidirect action is multiplication by 3 modulo 7. Both groups have order 6048 and totient sum 23984.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to research solved and replace answer(sorry) with answer(False), retaining the existing right-hand side. Add a reference to the negative solution.
